provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: the Tours Mame 1922 reads 'DomiM ne,' where the 1962 prints 'Domine,'; the Tours Mame 1922 window carries ':' at this point where the 1962 does not; the Tours Mame 1922 sets no pointing after 'exoramus' where the 1962 sets a colon; recogniser damage in the Tours Mame 1922 text layer at this locus, not variant readings: Domino for domine; AJESTATEM for maiestatem; stipplices for suplices; tuérum for tuorum; letificas; for laetificas; bare numeric tokens (printed folio / marginal numbers) dropped from the Tours Mame 1922 reading: 32, 1. 28 671 3, 1-2 3.; conclusion length was not collated: the 1962 prints 'Per Dominum.' and the witness abbreviates the same rubrical cue; one formula at two lengths, which is within the matched tolerance. Corroboration: Pustet Ratisbon 1862, nearest preceding printed-folio marker 532 at text-layer line 73173; text-layer lines 73259-73274 (char-level agreement 0.957 with the 1962 target).

propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Majestatem tuam, Domine, supplices exoramus: ut, sicut nos jugiter Sanctorum
tuorum commemoratione laetificas; ita semper supplicatione defendas. Per
Dominum.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Hostias, Domine, tuae plebis intende: et, quas in honore Sanctorum tuorum
devota mente celebrat, proficere sibi sentiat ad salutem. Per Dominum
nostrum.

propers.text:
Repleti, Domine, muneribus sacris: quaesumus; ut, intercedentibus Sanctis
tuis, in gratiarum semper actione maneamus. Per Dominum.
